summary.text: A supermassive black hole is the largest type of black hole, with a mass from hundreds of thousands to billions of times the Sun's.
Observations indicate that almost every large galaxy has one at its center, and the Milky Way's is the radio source Sagittarius A*.
Interstellar gas accreting onto these black holes is the process that powers active galactic nuclei and quasars.

facts.label: Mass range
facts.value: Hundreds of thousands to billions of Suns

facts.label: Directly imaged
facts.value: Two, by the Event Horizon Telescope

facts.label: Event horizon size
facts.value: Radius about 19 AU at a billion Suns

facts.label: Ultramassive
facts.value: Above 5 billion Suns, though the term is little used

items.prompt: Two travelers cross the event horizon, one of a small stellar-mass black hole and one of a 10 million Sun black hole. Who feels less stretching between head and feet?

options.label: The one entering the smaller, since less mass pulls less
The one entering the larger black hole, since its horizon force is far weaker
Both feel exactly the same stretch
Neither feels any stretch until deep inside

items.explain: Tidal force at the horizon falls with the square of the mass, so a person at the horizon of a 10 million Sun black hole feels about what a person on Earth's surface does.

items.prompt: A black hole is made 100 times more massive. How does its average density change?

options.label: It gets higher, since there is more mass inside
It stays the same, since volume grows with mass
It can go either way depending on spin
It gets lower, since the more massive hole has lower density

items.explain: The average density of a black hole is inversely proportional to the square of its mass, so higher mass black holes have lower average density.

items.prompt: A supermassive black hole sits quietly in a galaxy. What would make the galaxy's center blaze like a quasar?

options.label: The black hole shrinking in size
Stars in the galaxy forming in bulk
Interstellar gas accreting onto the black hole
The black hole merging with a star

items.explain: Accretion of interstellar gas onto supermassive black holes powers active galactic nuclei and quasars.

items.prompt: Two supermassive black holes have been directly imaged by the Event Horizon Telescope. Which pair?

options.label: Sagittarius A* and the hole at the center of Messier 87
The holes at the centers of Andromeda and Sombrero
TON 618 and Phoenix A
Sagittarius A* and TON 618

items.explain: The imaged black holes are Sagittarius A*, in the Milky Way, and the one at the center of the giant elliptical galaxy Messier 87.

items.prompt: Quasars put out huge energy from a tiny region. In 1964, what explanation did Salpeter and Zeldovich propose?

options.label: A very large star burning its hydrogen
Ordinary stars crowded together very closely
A collision between two galaxies at the center
Matter falling onto a massive compact object

items.explain: They proposed that matter falling onto a massive compact object would explain the properties of quasars.

items.prompt: Some scientists once thought quasars were powered by enormous hydrogen-burning objects. What was Richard Feynman's objection?

options.label: They would burn out in only a few short years
Past a critical mass they would be unstable and collapse into a black hole
They could never be bright enough to match quasars
They would blow apart the galaxies that host them

items.explain: Feynman noted that stars above a critical mass are dynamically unstable and would collapse into a black hole, at least if non-rotating.
